# Summary of Cairn System Rules

## Basic Pulse (C1)
When you pulse a cairn, it grows by more than just the stride amount. The growth formula is: new height = old height + stride + (count of full strides fitting in the old height). This creates accelerating growth—taller cairns benefit from bonus marks based on their current size.

## Repeated Pulses (C2)
Each pulse must be calculated fresh from the new height. You cannot use a shortcut by applying the same bonus repeatedly. After each pulse, you recalculate how many complete strides fit into the updated height, then pulse again from there.

## Leak (C3)
A leak removes marks after pulsing based on the new (post-pulse) height. You count how many complete leak units fit into the pulsed height and subtract that many marks. The leak depends entirely on the height the cairn reached after pulsing.

## Origin/Working Backwards (C4)
To find a starting height that leads to a known final height, you must reverse the pulse process step-by-step, not use arithmetic shortcuts. Different starting heights produce different pulse results because the bonus depends on height.

## Drain (C5)
In each cycle, a cairn pulses then loses a fixed drain amount. Because pulses add height-dependent bonuses, the drain doesn't prevent growth unless it eventually exceeds what the pulse adds. You simulate cycles until the height reaches zero or below.

## Merging (C6)
Two cairns combine using weighted shares and a tether connector. Each cairn contributes a portion (floor of share × height), and these portions add together plus the tether value to create the merged height.
